observations.contract: Changed manifest and new current typed errors
observations.trace: Historical6533 GPU manifest lacks a direct derive_more dependency; 95e adds derive_more2.1.1 with display and error features. The historical lock already lists derive_more2.1.1. Current texture view and validation scope error sources use that dependency to preserve selected typed native failures.
observations.remaining: Do not infer that every GPU failure uses these owners or that the dependency package itself is newly locked. Both manifest versions and exact historical provenance are preserved. No macro or GPU ran.

observations.trace: UniformMember retains only name, offset and size. The public create_bind_groups chooses encoding from the supplied parameter variant. Its Mat3 arm checks offset+member.size <= uniform-buffer length, sets col_stride=member.size/3, then writes three f32 components for each of three columns. Symbolically, for a caller-supplied public reflection member offset0,size12 in a 12-byte block and a matching-name Mat3 parameter, the guard passes and stride is4; at column1, row2 the code requests bytes12..16, beyond the 12-byte vector.
observations.remaining: Original151 already identified shared uniform ABI mismatch and delegate2331 had explicitly left Mat3 stride and bounds admission open. This conditional public-metadata example assumes an available context/layout and mismatched member/parameter; it does not establish a real shader or ordinary producer reaches it. The separate actual ComputePass and cached path have their own packers; do not generalize helper behavior to them. No reflection object, slice, shader, GPU or panic ran.

observations.trace: Buffer.write forwards an upload at offset0 directly to native queue.write_buffer, while write_at checks offset addition and the retained logical size first. from_upload allocates using the same upload length and requests COPY_DST.
observations.remaining: Original Adler157 already recorded the oversized write concern and the safe same-length from_upload path. A logical4-byte buffer plus8-byte upload would not get a wrapper extent rejection through write, but native validation, usage and alignment outcome remain unobserved. No buffer or queue ran.

observations.trace: Buffer.read formats a native map failure into text, drops the WASM map error object and ignores native poll results; the separate compute ReadbackError retains wgpu::BufferAsyncError and PollError sources. The pinned wgpu BufferAsyncError is a unit error type. The host Readback helper rejects zero-sized types, partial elements and truncated bytes before an aligned initialized copy.
observations.remaining: Original Adler158 explicitly applied alias records to the delegate native-map334 and WASM-map335 subcontracts only; preserve those identities and do not merge channel closure or host-copy reasons. Poll outcome policy, callers and runtime effects remain open. No error or readback ran.

observations.contract: Public buffer metadata and native authority
observations.trace: Buffer publicly exposes an Arc<wgpu::Buffer>, logical size and usage, and Clone shares the native buffer while copying the metadata fields. New initializes usage from the native buffer and requests its native allocation size from the same logical length. Subsequent public mutation or struct construction can make size or usage disagree; read branches on the wrapper usage and write_at checks wrapper size. Pinned wgpu exposes native size and usage accessors.
observations.remaining: A logical extent can intentionally differ from an allocation extent in some designs; the supported wrapper contract and externally constructed values need investigation. This is an authority/admission question with a conditional public-state example, not an observed native validation failure. No buffer or queue ran.

observations.contract: Separate closed bind and buffer reasons
observations.trace: Historical queue318–333 and336–338 name distinct first checks for layout, buffer, texture, sampler, extent, native/WASM channel and host-copy conditions. The selected source expresses these as separate anyhow prose, while the observed native mapping errors are different source-bearing operations.
observations.remaining: Keep each historical identity, branch and platform rather than inferring aliases from a common error type remedy. Whether each caller needs typed error handling remains open; no resource/error path ran.
